summary: The agent completed a substantial, legitimate implementation and preserved all baseline behavior, but the new suite failed 3 of 46 tests because string-keyed Guava BiMap attributes were treated as opaque rather than as descendable and updatable maps.
quick_failure_summary: String-keyed BiMap attributes reject key traversal and updates instead of behaving like supported maps.

details.reasoning: The implementation deliberately recognizes a descendable string-keyed map only when ValueAttribute.typeKind().isPlainMapKind() is true. That excludes Guava BiMap even when its keys are String. Consequently, resolving /pairs/k/label produces PointerTypeException, resolving /pairs/absent produces PointerTypeException instead of PointerMissException, and updating /pairs/k/label is rejected before the operator can run. The reference implementation instead accepts any map type except multimap and sorted map when the key type is String, matching the prompt.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's added tests exercised java.util.Map<String, ...> but did not include another string-keyed Map subtype such as BiMap, so its focused suite passed despite the over-restrictive classification. The rest of the hidden feature suite passed 43 of 46 tests.

justification.issue_description: The generated companion must traverse and update map attributes with String keys, including BiMap<String, V>; the agent restricted support to metadata classified as a plain map.
justification.evidence: The prompt says a step selecting a 'map attribute with plain string keys' uses the following step as the key, and later enumerates the opaque cases as 'multimap, sorted or non-string-keyed map' without excluding BiMap. In PointersGenerator.java, isStringMap requires both attribute.isMapType() and attribute.typeKind().isPlainMapKind(), while the visible metadata API separately exposes isMapType(), isMultimapType(), and isSortedMapType(). The reference model uses those explicit exclusions and a String-key check rather than isPlainMapKind().
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT because the required behavior was stated in the prompt and was implementable using visible metadata distinctions. It is not an undocumented hidden-test convention: the hidden tests merely expose the agent's narrower-than-specified interpretation by using BiMap<String, Element>.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is broad and processor-heavy but solvable, as demonstrated by the reference solution and the agent passing most feature cases. The map inclusion/exclusion rule is explicit, and the three failures consistently exercise one deterministic classification defect.

evidence: JUnit reports show the baseline suite passed 326/326 and the new suite executed normally, passing 43/46 with three assertion/runtime failures in generated pointer behavior.
All three new-test failures point to /pairs on an unmodified BiMap fixture and correspond directly to the agent's isPlainMapKind() restriction.
The trajectory shows rg was unavailable, but the agent immediately switched to find/grep and continued; this did not prevent implementation or validation.

The trajectory also shows the agent resolved intermediate shading and packaged-processor compilation issues and ultimately ran its pointer tests, processor tests, and integration compilation successfully.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker or verifier defect was found; the verifier exposed a localized implementation omission in string-keyed map subtype handling.
